final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and instead reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing improves accuracy and removes some overstatement, but it does not cure the core defect: the admissible evidence still shows a material limitation affecting a named launch use case, an open legal question on disclosure, and no evidence of disclosure completion, remediation, or approved risk acceptance. A caveated readiness narrative may be descriptively fair as an operational summary, but it is not enough for compliant_with_caveats here because the unresolved caveat is itself the missing compliance predicate under the release policy. The Actor's narrowed position is therefore less overbroad than before, yet the certification claim remains unsupported on the present evidence.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence resolves the policy predicate requiring disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance for a material limitation in a named launch use case.
The developer-support migration segment remains below target and is explicitly named in launch commitments, so materiality remains live under the policy text.
Legal review is still open, which leaves the disclosure obligation unresolved rather than satisfied.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational stability but do not authorize certification in place of the specific policy requirement.
Public model-card and AI risk-management guidance support documentation and monitoring practices, but they do not substitute for internal policy compliance.
